items.title: Connascence 101
items.summary: What makes software difficult to change? Often, it's the dependencies between different parts of the code.**Connascence** provides a more precise vocabulary for understanding and reasoning about coupling, cohesion, and software design.In this introductory talk, we'll explore the different types of connascence (static and dynamic), their properties (strength, degree, and locality), and practical guidelines for identifying design problems and making better refactoring decisions.The goal isn't to introduce yet another set of rigid rules, but to discover a useful tool for discussing software design, making informed trade-offs, and building software that's easier to understand, test, and evolve.Ultimately, it's about what really matters: **enabling the continuous and sustainable delivery of value.**
